back: Hardware that captures data from users or the environment and converts it into digital form for the computer.
Red light shone on the code; white reflects, black absorbs; sensor detects the pattern; converted to a digital number; product looked up in a database.
A camera captures the 2D pattern; software uses the three corner squares to find position and decodes the data (e.g. a URL).
LED lights the surface; tiny camera takes hundreds of images a second; processor compares them to find direction and distance.
Sound vibrates a diaphragm → varying electrical signal (analogue) → ADC → digital data.
Pressure pushes two conductive layers together, completing a circuit. Works with gloves; easily scratched.
A conductive finger changes the charge on the coated glass. Clear and multi-touch; no ordinary gloves.
A touch breaks a grid of infra-red beams. Works with any object and large screens; dust or insects may trigger it.
2D: copies flat documents into an image (OCR can make text editable). 3D: measures a solid object's shape to make a 3D model.
Lens → image sensor of millions of light-sensitive cells → electrical signals → digital pixel values stored on a memory card.
